findings.title: Kullukta çekişen yetki
findings.claim: The focus word عَبْدًا can hold the praying figure within a wider contest over belonging: the servant is named through owned status, voluntary worship, and humanly imposed enslavement as distinct pressures returning to the same focus carrier.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier 96:10:1:1 meets 16:75's owned-servant wording, 1:5's exclusive worship wording, and 26:22's forced-enslavement wording. These independent wider contacts change the reading of the praying servant from a bare role label into the point where divine-facing devotion and human control meet.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the servant's identity matters to the prohibition: the act is performed by one whose allegiance is already legible, while another authority tries to control that allegiance.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading remains a servant praying. This finding adds an authority relation; it does not assert that the focus figure's historical legal status is identical to the wider owned or enslaved examples.

epistemic.reason: Trusted focus-anchored publication support supplies the complete claim, while the cross-ayah contacts and their application to the focus are a bounded contextual inference and target morphology is not supplied.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Kişi özgürün karşıtı olarak bir başkasının mülkiyetinde bulunur.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus noun عَبْدًا names the concrete servant figure and can carry an owned-person status under the supplied branch.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Connection conn_b7fa28821f0e69b0142c supplies the wider phrase عَبْدًا مَّمْلُوكًا in 16:75, an explicit owned-servant occurrence.
branch_activations.activation: The wider owned-servant occurrence contacts the focus servant noun, making belonging and human control perceptible within the focus scene without changing its ordinary servant reference.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The praying servant is also visible as the location of a contested claim over whom a person belongs to.
branch_activations.boundary: This activates the owned-status pressure as a contextual resonance; it does not assign the focus figure a specific legal status.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Eylem, sıradan itaati aşan bir boyun eğme ve alçalma tutumu içerir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus noun عَبْدًا identifies a servant whose role can be heard as enacted submission and worship.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Connection conn_f8ad0d8588d5fa2be644 supplies the exclusive worship wording إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ in 1:5.
branch_activations.activation: The exclusive worship formulation gives the focus servant a divine-facing direction, so the prohibition can be read against an already enacted allegiance.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The servant is not only someone being controlled; he is someone voluntarily oriented in worship, which makes the attempted interference an authority conflict.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus remains a servant in the ordinary scene; the wider exclusive-devotion wording supplies direction without replacing the local grammar.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: köleleştirmek veya köle gibi boyunduruk altına almak
branch_activations.facet_statement: Eyleyen, başka bir insanı köle edinir veya köle durumuna getirir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus noun عَبْدًا is the servant carrier through which an imposed subjection pressure can be heard.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Connection conn_df0be55f29c3f104deb4 supplies the forced-enslavement wording عَبَّدتَّ بَنِي إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ in 26:22.
branch_activations.activation: The wider forced-enslavement occurrence contacts the focus servant designation and supplies the humanly imposed pole of the authority relation.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The prohibition becomes legible as an attempt to place human control over a servant's already directed submission.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus does not thereby assert a new legal event; the branch is used for the supplied coercive contrast only.

findings.title: Namazın beden ve yakarış olarak iki yönü
findings.claim: The focus verb صَلَّىٰ remains performed prayer, while its wider lexical contact also lets the act be heard as a directed appeal for good and mercy under pressure.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier 96:10:3:1 meets the guarded bodily-prayer sequence in 4:102 and the supplicatory construction in 9:103. The two wider contacts make the prohibition touch both the concrete performance and the outward appeal carried by the same focus verb.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees why a translation's single word namaz leaves something unheard: the act has bodily form and a directed, mercy-seeking address that becomes newly relevant when it is obstructed.
findings.containment: The local Form II verb still describes the servant's performed prayer. The wider supplicatory use does not assign the focus servant a divine or messenger subject and does not erase the ritual reading.

epistemic.reason: Trusted publication support names both supplied branches; the wider contacts provide exact Arabic but no target morphology, so their application is retained as a bounded contextual inference.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: başkası için iyilik dileme; esirgeme, övme ve değer verme
branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir kişi başkası için iyilik, esenlik ve iyi sonuç diler.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus verb صَلَّىٰ is the act performed by the servant and can carry a directed good-wishing or supplicatory relation in the wider branch.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Connection conn_f33c83addffbf7d595f6 supplies صَلِّ عَلَيْهِمْ and صَلَوَٰتُكَ سَكَنٌۭ لَّهُمْ in 9:103, an explicit outward-directed prayer construction.
branch_activations.activation: The wider directed-prayer construction contacts the focus verb, so the act under prohibition can be heard as an appeal whose outward good-wishing dimension is also being interrupted.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Prayer becomes a directed appeal for good and settling mercy alongside its performed form.
branch_activations.boundary: Only the human good-wishing facet is activated here; the focus subject is not recast as God or an angel, and ritual prayer remains present.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: ayakta durma, eğilme ve yere kapanma bölümleri olan kurallı tapınma
branch_activations.facet_statement: Kuralları belirlenmiş tapınma, ayakta durma, eğilme, yere kapanma, dilek ve yüceltme bölümlerini içerir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus verb صَلَّىٰ carries the performed act of the servant's ordered prayer.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Connection conn_c1f3237bfb0d82d6026d supplies a guarded prayer sequence in 4:102 with standing, prostration, repeated prayer, and weapons kept ready.
branch_activations.activation: The wider guarded sequence gives bodily performance and vulnerability a concrete contact point, making the focus prohibition concern an embodied practice rather than an abstract label.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The praying act is seen as a complete, bodily discipline that can continue even while its surrounding situation is dangerous or contested.
branch_activations.boundary: The wider guarded sequence is a contextual parallel, not a claim that the focus supplies its military details or every ritual condition.

findings.title: Seçilmiş boyun eğme ile zorlanan boyun eğdirme
findings.claim: The focus servant can be read through a contrast of agency: worshipful lowering is chosen, while the wider forced-enslavement occurrence supplies lowering imposed by another human power.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier 96:10:1:1 meets 1:5's exclusive worship and 26:22's forced-enslavement wording. Their contact changes the servant designation from a generic status into an agency contrast in which the same field of submission can be entered willingly or imposed coercively.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel the difference between a servant who lowers himself in worship and a person whom another agent tries to lower by force; the prohibition thus carries a reversal of agency without replacing the plain scene.
findings.containment: This finding retains the ordinary servant-praying scene and states an added agency contrast. The candidate's supplied B005 road/tarred-animal/coated-ship branch is excluded and is not used to define coercion.

epistemic.reason: Trusted publication support supplies the voluntary-versus-coercive relation, while the focus-to-context contrast is an explicit bounded inference from exact wider occurrences whose target morphology is not supplied.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Eylem, sıradan itaati aşan bir boyun eğme ve alçalma tutumu içerir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus noun عَبْدًا carries the worshipful submission relation of a servant who is oriented toward obedience.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Connection conn_f8ad0d8588d5fa2be644 supplies exclusive worship toward God in 1:5, while conn_df0be55f29c3f104deb4 supplies the contrasting forced-enslavement occurrence in 26:22.
branch_activations.activation: The exclusive-devotion and forced-enslavement contacts place the focus servant's submission on an agency axis, making chosen worship perceptibly different from being made subject by another.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The servant's lowering remains voluntary in its worship direction while the surrounding authority conflict exposes the opposite possibility of imposed subjection.
branch_activations.boundary: No root_000973/B005 road or tarred-animal facet is activated; the coercive pole is a contextual contrast supplied by 26:22, not a relabeling of B005.

findings.title: Baskı altında kulluk ve yakarış
findings.claim: When the focus servant is heard through both worshipful servanthood and directed prayer, the prohibition touches two connected forms of allegiance at once: enacted submission and an appeal made toward good and mercy.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers 96:10:1:1 and 96:10:3:1 are contacted by 1:5's exclusive worship wording, 9:103's outward-directed prayer wording, and 5:91's explicit adversarial turning-away from prayer. The contacts make the restriction operate on both the servant's allegiance and the prayer's communicative reach.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the forbidden act as a living relation under pressure: prayer is bodily worship and outward address, while the servant's direction of obedience is also being challenged.
findings.containment: The plain reading remains a servant praying when the prohibition operates. The finding joins only the two anchored components of the reader-walk composite; its proposed snare branch and unresolved ر ح م/B001 and ق ر ء/B006 citations are not carried.

epistemic.reason: The legacy reader-walk support explicitly states the combined servant, worship, and prayer mechanism, while the registered branches and wider contacts provide a bounded reconstruction; unresolved cited roots remain outside the finding.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Eylem, sıradan itaati aşan bir boyun eğme ve alçalma tutumu içerir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus servant noun عَبْدًا carries enacted submission and worship, while the focus relation places that servant under attempted restraint.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Connection conn_f8ad0d8588d5fa2be644 supplies exclusive worship toward God in 1:5, and conn_cd79435142573aa6c88f supplies an adversarial force turning people away from prayer in 5:91.
branch_activations.activation: The wider exclusive-devotion and obstruction contacts meet the focus servant carrier, so the prohibition can be seen as pressure on a chosen allegiance rather than only interruption of an isolated action.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The servant's worship becomes the visible point where divine-facing submission is challenged by an opposing human or adversarial pressure.
branch_activations.boundary: The finding does not identify the focus opponent with the adversarial agent of 5:91 or add a new actor to the local grammar.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: başkası için iyilik dileme; esirgeme, övme ve değer verme
branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir kişi başkası için iyilik, esenlik ve iyi sonuç diler.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus verb صَلَّىٰ carries the praying act whose directed appeal can be heard through the supplied branch.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Connection conn_f33c83addffbf7d595f6 supplies outward-directed prayer for others in 9:103, while conn_cd79435142573aa6c88f supplies explicit opposition to prayer in 5:91.
branch_activations.activation: The outward-directed prayer contact meets the focus act precisely where the wider obstruction contact gives that act an adversarial pressure, so the prohibition reaches the prayer's communicative direction as well as its bodily performance.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The forbidden prayer is also a good-wishing appeal whose reach is being blocked under pressure.
branch_activations.boundary: Only the human good-wishing facet is retained; divine and angelic subject specializations, and the rejected snare branch, are not inferred.

findings.title: Sonraki secdeyle gelen cevap
findings.claim: The later supplied context of 96:19 answers the attempted stopping of the servant's prayer with commanded prostration and nearness, so the focus act is reread as continuing and intensifying under pressure.
findings.mechanism: The retrospective support returns through the focus's praying-servant act and names 96:19's واسجد واقترب as the later response. The contact changes the prohibition from a possible endpoint into a setting in which the devotional act continues through a more concentrated bodily approach.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive the focus prayer as an act whose later answer is renewed nearness, so the pressure around it does not exhaust what the act does.
findings.containment: This is a branchless retrospective contextual reading. It does not claim that 96:10 itself contains the words for prostration or nearness, and it does not adjudicate the wider historical sequence beyond the supplied reader-walk statement.

epistemic.reason: The legacy reader-walk explicitly records the later 96:19 change and focus return, but the packet supplies no normalized branch activation or exact later-word trace.
